claim: For every odd \(n>3\), let \(B_n\) be the automaton on \(Q=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(b(i)=i+1\pmod n\), \(a(i)=i\) for \(i<n-1\), \(a(n-1)=1\), and \(a(n)=2\). Define \(\lambda_n(s)=\min\{|w|:|Qw|\le n-s\}\). For every \(1\le s\le(n+1)/2\), \(\lambda_n(1)=1\); for every \(k\ge0\) with \(2k+2\le(n+1)/2\), \(\lambda_n(2k+2)=5k+1\); and for every \(k\ge1\) with \(2k+1\le(n+1)/2\), \(\lambda_n(2k+1)=5k\). Sharp witnesses are \(a(b^4a)^k\) for deficiency \(2k+2\) and \(ab^3a(b^4a)^{k-1}\) for deficiency \(2k+1\).
integrity: The infinite claim is supported by an elementary proof from the stated transition rules. Exact finite BFS and witness replay are reproducibility checks only. No independent external audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to odd \(n>3\) and deficiencies at most \((n+1)/2\). It does not determine later intermediate ranks or classify all shortest words. Finite BFS is used only as a stress test, not as proof. Literature search cannot establish absolute novelty; equivalent older terminology remains a residual bibliographic risk.
title: Exact initial rank-compression thresholds of the bactrian automata \(B_n\)
